 Judgment

1) The appellant has called in question judgment dated 09.02.2019 passed by the learned Principal District Judge, Anantnag, whereby, in a reference against the award passed by the Collector Land Acquisition, Anantnag (respondent No.2 herein), compensation for acquired land has been enhanced from Rs.8.00 lacs to Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal besides holding that the quantum of acquired land belonging to respondent No.1 is 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai instead of 02 kanals 03 marlas and 01 sirsai.

2) The facts emanating from the record are that the appellant (Indenting Department) issued an indent for acquisition of land in connection with construction/four lanning of National Highway at Villages Sransoo, Shampora, Qazigund Tehsil Dooru in terms of communication No.PD/JMU/2294 dated 28.12.2005.

Pursuant to the aforesaid communication, respondent No.2, the Collector, issued notification under Section 4 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Act")
vide No.LA/Ang/LA/Ang/1154-57 dated 12.01.2008 for acquisition of land measuring 108 kanals,
05 marlas and 04 sirsai situated at aforesaid village.
Declaration under Section 6 and 7 the Act was issued vide communication dated 28.01.2008 and notice under Section 9 and 9A the Act was issued thereafter.

sentences.text: The final award was passed by the Collector vide No.87- 90/LA/Ang dated 23.04.2011.
It is pertinent to mention here that the Collector has, in the instant case, invoked urgency clause under Section 17 of the Act.
Vide the award dated 23.04.2011, the Collector assessed the compensation of the acquired land @Rs.8.00 lacs per kanal with Jabirana @15%.

4) It seems that respondent No.1, whose land was also subject matter of acquisition, made an application before the Collector in terms of Section 18 of the Act claiming therein that actual quantum of land belonging to him that was subject matter of acquisition, is 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai but as per the award, compensation for land measuring 02 kanals 03 marlas and 01 sirsai only has been assessed in his favour.

It was also claimed in the said application that the market value of the acquired land is Rs.1.20 lacs per marla but the Collector has fixed the market value of the acquired land @Rs.8.00 lacs per kanal only.
The aforesaid application was made by respondent No.1 before the Collector on 10th July, 2013.
5) Respondent No.2, the Collector, vide his communication dated 17.07.2013 made a reference to District Judge, Anantnag, in terms of Section 18/31 of the Act.
It is in these circumstances that the matter landed before the learned District Judge, Anantnag.

6) Before the Reference Court, the Collector and the Indenting Department (the appellants herein)
were impleaded as respondents.

The Reference Court vide order dated 13.05.2015 framed the following issues:
(I) Whether the petitioner was owner and possession of land measuring 2 kanals 14 marlas and 3 sarsaie under survey No.133/133 min, 135/135 min, 134/134 min and 136/136 min situated in village Shampora Qazigund acquired for four lanning of National Highway by Collector?
OPP (II) Whether petitioner, being owner of land comprising of survey Nos.134/134 min and 136/136 min has not been awarded compensation thereof?
OPP (III) Whether the petitioner is entitled to get compensation at the rate of Rs.1.20 lacs per marla for his acquired land?
OPP (IV) Whether reference in hand is not maintainable in the present form and is liable to be rejected?

OPP (V) Relief.
7)

After framing of the issues, respondent No.1, the land owner, besides examining himself as a witness, examined PWs Abdul Gaffar Mir, Ghulam Jeelani, Ghulam Mohi-ud- din Itoo and Abdul Hamid, in support of his case.
However, no evidence was led either by the Collector or by the appellant Indenting Department.

After closure of the evidence of the parties, the learned Reference Court in terms of impugned judgment/award dated 09.02.2019 came to the conclusion that the quantum of land belonging to respondent No.1 that has been actually acquired is 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai and the market value of the land in question on the crucial date was Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.
Accordingly, compensation in the amount of Rs.43,46,666/ with 15% Jabirana along with interest @7% has been awarded in favour of respondent No.1.

sentences.text: The appellant has challenged the impugned award/judgment on the grounds that the learned Presiding Officer, prior to the date of passing the impugned award/judgment, had been attached with the High Court and his request for voluntary retirement from service was accepted by the Government with effect from 04.01.2019 and, as such, the impugned award/judgment is a nullity.

It has been also contended that the reference was time barred as the award was passed by the Collector on 23.04.2011 whereas the reference was made by him after more than two years on 17.07.2013 but the learned Reference Court has erroneously concluded that the Reference Court has no jurisdiction to dismiss the reference on the ground of limitation.

It has also been contended that while enhancing compensation, the learned Reference Court has relied upon contradictory evidence tendered by respondent No.1, the land owner, and, in fact, there was no cogent material before the Reference Court to award enhanced compensation.
It has been further contended that the finding of the Reference Court regarding quantum of land is imaginary based on no evidence.

9) I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the grounds of challenge, the impugned award, record of the Reference Court and the record of the Collector.
10) Learned counsel for respondent No.1, the land owner, has raised a preliminary objection to the maintainability of the appeal by contending that the appellant Indenting Department does not have any locus standi to file the appeal against the impugned award without obtaining leave of the Court.
In this regard, the learned counsel has relied upon the ratio laid down by a Single Bench of this Court in the case titled National Highway Authority of India vs. Ali Mohammad Dar and anr. (CFA No.190/2014 decided on25.08.2022).
11) On the other hand, learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant-Indenting Department was a party/respondent before the Reference Court, as such, it has a statutory right to file an appeal against the impugned award.
12) In the above context, the provisions contained in Section 48 of the Act, which is in pari materia with the provisions contained in Section 50 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, are required to be noticed.

It reads as under:
48. Acquisition of land at cost of a local body, person or body of persons. -(1) When the provisions of this Act are put in force for the purpose of acquiring land and at the cost of any fund controlled or managed by a local body or of any person or body of persons, whether corporate or not, the charges of and incidental to, such acquisition shall be defrayed from or by such fund or such person or body of persons.
(2) In any proceedings held before a Collector or Court in such cases the local authority or the person or the body of persons concerned may appear and adduce evidence for the purpose of determining the amount of compensation :
Provided that, no such person or a body of persons shall be entitled to demand a reference under section National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/

From a perusal of sub-section (2) quoted above

sentences.text: , it appears that a local authority or the person or the body of persons at whose cost the land is being acquired, has a right to appear and adduce evidence for the purpose of determining the amount of compensation, both before the Collector as well as before the Reference Court.

13) A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of UP Awas Evam Vikas Parishad vs.
Gyan Devi & Ors, (1995) 2 SCC 326, while, considering the provisions contained in Section 50(2) of 1894 Act, concluded that a local authority, for whom the land is being acquired, has a right to participate in the proceedings for acquisition before the Collector as well as before the Reference Court and to adduce evidence for the purpose of determining the amount of compensation and the said right imposes an obligation on the Collector as well as the Reference Court to give a notice to the local authority with regard to the pendency of those proceedings and the date on which the matter regarding determination of amount of compensation would be taken up.

sentences.text:
Thus, the Indenting Department is a proper party in the proceedings before the Collector as well as before the Reference Court and it is entitled to be impleaded as a party in the proceedings before the Reference Court.
14)
In view of the aforesaid position of law, the appellant was rightly impleaded as a party/respondent in the proceedings before the Reference Court.

The question that falls for determination is as to whether the appellant in the capacity of a party to the proceedings before the Reference Court is entitled to file an appeal against the award passed by the Reference Court or it has to obtain leave before maintaining the appeal against the award of the Reference Court.

15) The learned Coordinate Bench of this Court in Ali Mohammad Dar's case (supra) has, after relying upon the ratio laid down by the Supreme Court in UP Awas Evam Vikas Parishad's case (supra), concluded that before maintaining an appeal, the Indenting Department/local authority has to obtain leave of the Court for filing an appeal once it is shown that the Government has not filed any appeal against the award of the Reference Court.

This opinion of the Coordinate Bench is solely based upon the observations made by the Supreme Court in UP Awas Evam Vikas Parishad's case (supra),
16) If we analyse the facts of the case that were subject matter of consideration before the Supreme Court in UP Awas Evam Vikas Parishad's case (supra), as narrated in para (25) of the said judgment,
it comes to the fore that notice under sub-section (2) of Section 50 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, was not served on the Board either by the Land Acquisition Officer or by the Tribunal.
The Board did not feel aggrieved by the award made by the Land Acquisition Officer or the Tribunal.
The Board only felt aggrieved by the decision of the High Court in first appeal whereby the amount of compensation was enhanced.

It is in the backdrop of said facts that the Supreme Court held that the applications of the Board for being impleaded as respondent in the appeals filed by the land owners before the High Court deserve to be allowed.

17) The Supreme Court in para (22) of the same judgement has explained the right of a local authority to file an appeal, in the following manner:
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
4 22.

sentences.text: In case the amount of compensation has been enhanced by the court and no appeal is filed by the Government the local authority if adversely affected by such enhancement may file an appeal with the leave of the court.
This right of the local authority does not depend on its being impleaded as a party in the proceedings before the reference court.

Even if the local authority is not impleaded as a party before the reference court it can file an appeal against the award of the reference court in the High Court after obtaining leave if it is prejudicially affected by the award.
In case the Government files an appeal against the enhancement of the award the local authority is entitled to support the said appeal and get itself impleaded as a party.

When the person having an interest in the land files an appeal in the High Court against the award of the reference court and seeks enhancement of the amount of compensation the local authority should be impleaded as a party in the said appeal and it is entitled to be served with the notice of the said appeal so that it can defend the award of the reference court and oppose enhancement of the amount of compensation before the High Court.
The same will be the situation in case of an appeal to this Court from the decision of the High Court.

18) In para (24) of the judgment, the Supreme Court summed up its conclusions as under:
24.

To sum up, our conclusions are:
1. Section 50(2) of the L.A. Act confers on a local authority for whom land is being acquired a right to appear in the acquisition proceedings before the Collector and the reference court and adduce evidence for the purpose of determining the amount of compensation.
2. The said right carries with it the right to be given adequate notice by the Collector as well as the reference court before whom acquisition proceedings are pending on the date on which the matter of determination of compensation will be taken up.
3.

The proviso to Section 50(2) only precludes a local authority from seeking a reference but it does not deprive the local authority which feels aggrieved by the determination of the amount of compensation by the Collector or by the reference court to invoke the remedy under Article 226 of the Constitution as well as the remedies available under the L.A. Act.

4. In the event of denial of the right conferred by Section 50(2) on account of failure of the Collector to serve notice of the acquisition proceedings, the local authority can invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution.

5. Even when notice has been served on the local authority the remedy under Article 226 of the Constitution would be available to the local authority on grounds on which judicial review is permissible under Article 226.

5 6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The local authority is a proper party in the proceedings before the reference court and is entitled to be impleaded as a party in those proceedings wherein it can defend the determination of the amount of compensation by the Collector and oppose enhancement of the said amount and also adduce evidence in that regard.

7. In the event of enhancement of the amount of compensation by the reference court if the Government does not file an appeal, the local authority can file an appeal against the award in the High Court after obtaining leave of the court.

8. In an appeal by the person having an interest in land seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the reference court, the local authority should be impleaded as a party and is entitled to be served notice of the said appeal.
This would apply to an appeal in the High Court as well as in this Court.
9. Since a company for whom land is being acquired has the same right as a local authority under Section 50(2), whatever has been said with regard to a local authority would apply to a company too.
10. The matters which stand finally concluded will, however, not be reopened.

19) From a conjoint reading of the conclusions arrived at by the Supreme Court in para (24) and the observations made in para (22) of the aforesaid judgment, as quoted above, it is clear that right of a local authority to file an appeal does not depend on its being impleaded as party in the proceedings before the Reference Court.

The Supreme Court has clearly explained that even if a local authority is not impleaded as party before the Reference Court, it can file an appeal against the award of Reference Court in the High Court after obtaining leave if it is prejudicially affected by the award,
meaning thereby that if the local authority is not impleaded as a party, then it has to seek leave for assailing the award of the Reference Court.
However, the situation would be different if the local authority is a party to the proceedings before the Reference Court.

In that case, the local authority,
as a matter of right, is entitled to file an appeal against the award of the Reference Court like any other party in a civil suit without obtaining leave of the Court.

20) Section 52 of the Act, which relates to appeals, clearly provides that an appeal shall lie to the State High Court from any part of the award of the Court and the right of filing of appeal would be subject to the provisions of law in force relating to the procedure in civil section applicable to appeals from original decrees, which means that the procedure prescribed in Civil Procedure Code in respect of the appeals from original decrees would be applicable to such appeals.
Thus, provisions contained in Section 96 and Order 41 of the CPC would be applicable in relation to appeals against the award of Reference Court.
As per these provisions of CPC, a party to a suit has a right to file an appeal.
On the analogy of these provisions, a party before the Reference Court is vested with a right to file appeal against the award passed by the Reference Court without seeking leave of the Court.

21) It seems that the aforesaid legal position has escaped the notice of learned Coordinate Bench while holding that a local authority has to seek leave to file appeal even in a case where it was a party National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: before the Reference Court.
Therefore, the judgment of the learned Coordinate Bench being per in curium, is not a binding precedent.
22) In view of the foregoing discussion, the objection of learned counsel for respondent No.1 with regard to maintainability of the appeal is not sustainable.
Accordingly, the appeal is held to be maintainable.

23) It has been contended by learned counsel for the appellant that the learned Presiding Officer of the Reference Court was attached with the High Court even prior to passing of the impugned award and that his request for voluntary retirement had been accepted by the Government with retrospective effect, which means that as on the date of passing of the impugned award, he had ceased to be in service.
On this basis it has been contended that the impugned award is a nullity.

24) The record shows that the learned Presiding Officer had applied for voluntary retirement on 04.01.2019 and in terms of Government Order No.1071-LD(A) of 2019 dated 06.03.2019, his request was accepted with effect from 04.01.2019.

However, it also appears that vide order No.LD(A)2019/19 dated 11.06.2019, a corrigendum was issued to Government Order dated 06.03.2019 (supra) whereby it was provided that instead of 'with effect from 04.01.2019" the words "with immediate effect" may be read in the aforesaid Government Order, meaning thereby that voluntary retirement of the Presiding Officer was accepted on the date of issuance of Order dated 06.03.2019 and not from the date of submission of his application for voluntary retirement viz.
04.01.2019.
Thus, as on date of passing of the impugned award, the learned Presiding Officer was holding the office of District Judge, Anantnag, and he had not ceased to be the District Judge.

Thus,
the impugned judgment passed by the Reference Court is valid.
The contention of the appellant in this regard is without any merit.

25) It has been contended by learned counsel for the appellant that the reference made by the Collector at the instance of respondent No.1 was barred by time, inasmuch as the award has been passed on 23.04.2011 and the reference has been made by the Collector on 17.07.2013.

26) In the above context, it is to be noted that the learned Reference Court has, while dealing with this aspect of the matter, held that the Reference Court cannot return the reference on the ground of limitation.

It has been observed by the Reference Court that submission of reference by the Collector to the Court would mean that the delay, if any in filing the application under Section 18 of the Act is condoned.
27) That aforesaid observation of the learned Reference Court is definitely not in accordance with the law.

Once an objection with regard to limitation is raised by a party before the Reference Court,
an issue in this regard has to be framed and the Reference Court has to address this issue on merits.
Merely, because a reference has been made by the Collector does not mean that the delay stands condoned.

In the instant case, the Reference Court had specifically framed an issue with regard to maintainability of the reference and this would include the maintainability on the ground of limitation but the learned Reference Court has simply avoided decision on this issue, which is not in accordance with law.

National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/

sentences.text: The issue of limitation is, therefore, required to be gone into by this Court in the present appeal.

As per the provisions contained in Section 18 of the Act, an application for reference has to be made within six weeks from the date of Collector's award, if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when the award is made.
In other cases, it has to be made within six weeks of the receipt of notice from the Collector or within six months from the date of Collector's award.

29) In the instant case, respondent No.1 made an application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference, on 10th July, 2013, which is beyond the period of six months, the outer limit provided under Section 18 of the Act.
The question that arises for determination is as to whether the application for reference made by respondent No.1, the land owner, is time barred.
30) In the above context, if we have a look at the award, it has been passed by the Collector on 23.04.2011.

Copies of the award have been endorsed to the Financial Commissioner, Revenue, J&K,
Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir, and Project Director, NH1A, Jammu, for information.
There is nothing in the record to suggest that respondent No.1, the land owner, was present before the Collector at the time of passing of the award.
Thus, neither copy of the award was endorsed to him nor he was present at the time of passing of the award.

31) Section 12(2) of the Act casts a duty upon the Collector to give notice of the award to those interested persons who are not either personally present or represented before him at the time of making of award.

The period of six months prescribed in Section 18 of the Act in the case of a person who was not present before the Collector at the time of making of award, either in person or through his agent, would commence from the actual or constructive knowledge of making of the award.
Mere knowledge of pendency of acquisition proceedings or of notifications under Section 4 and 6 or any public notice would not mean notice of making of the award.

This Court in the case of State through Collector Land Acquisition vs. Probodh Chander and Ors. 2003 (2) JKJ 554, has, while interpreting as to what would constitute knowledge of the award, observed as under:
"7.

entities.text: State through Collector Land Acquisition vs. Probodh Chander and Ors. 2003 (2) JKJ 554
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, the knowledge of the award did not mean mere Knowledge of the fact that award had been made.
It must mean knowledge of the essential contents of the award.

The appellant has not placed any material on record in discharge of onus to prove that notice of making of the award as envisaged by Section 12(2) was served upon the claimants or that either the owners or their representatives were present at the time when award was made.
It is not disputed that the owners had received the compensation under protest in respect of the land acquired by the Collector on 17.3.1987.
An application for reference was filed by the claimants on that date.

This clearly shows that in the absence of any evidence oral or documentary placed on record by the appellant to the contrary, the knowledge about the two awards for all intents and purposes of the Act shall be attributed to the owners only on 17.3.1987,

On facts, it is established that the application for making a reference was definitely made within six months from the date of the knowledge of the award and the reference made by the Collector, Land Acquisition, cannot be held to be barred by time under Section 18 of the Act, as vouched strenuously by appellants, counsel, Mr.
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
8 B.S. Manhas, in his debate during arguments.
32) From the foregoing analysis of law on the subject, it is clear that in the absence of any evidence to show that a land owner making reference had the knowledge of the essential contents of the award, the knowledge to such land owner shall be attributed only when the amount of compensation has been offered to him.
33) In the instant case, as already indicated, neither the award was made in presence of respondent NO.1 nor any notice was given to him in terms of Section 12(2) of the Act, as such, it cannot be stated that the time of filing application for reference would run against him from the date of the award.

entities.text: National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The knowledge of making the award can be attributed to respondent No.1 only when the Collector offered him the compensation assessed under the award.
It is not discernible from the record of the Collector as to when the compensation was offered to respondent No.1.

The burden of proof regarding issue of maintainability of the reference as framed by the Reference Court, was upon the appellant, as such, it was for the appellant to prove that the reference was time barred.
In the absence of any material evidence in this regard, the appellant has failed to discharge this burden.
In these circumstances, the application for reference made by respondent No.1 before the Collector is held to be within time.
34) That takes us to the merits of the impugned award.

So for as the quantum of land belonging to respondent No.1, that has been acquired by the Collector for use by the appellant, is concerned, it is to be noted that respondent No.1 in support of his contention that actual quantum of land that had come under acquisition is 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai, has relied upon the report of Tehsildar, Mark "A" and the statement of Tehsildar, PW Ghulam Mohi-ud- din.

As per report Mark "A", land measuring 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai belonging to respondent No.1 has been utilized for construction of National Highway Bypass which is comprised in Khasra Nos.133/133-min, 135/135-min, 134/134-min and 136/136-min.

35) The Tehsildar in his statement has deposed that on 19.01.2009, Naib Tehsildar, Qazigund was asked to undertake measurements of the land belonging to respondent No.1 that had come under acquisition.
This was done at the instance of respondent No.1, who had made an application that his excess land to the extent of 11 marlas and 02 sirsai has come under acquisition.

On the basis of his directions, the Naib Tehsildar, after undertaking measurement of the land, submitted his report in which it was indicated that land measuring 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai owned and possessed by respondent No.1 has come under acquisition whereas initially, when the measurement of the land was undertaken, the quantum of land belonging to respondent No.1, that had come under acquisition, was shown as 02 kanals 03 marlas and 01 sirsai only.
He further deposed that he attested the report dated 15.01.2009 on 19.01.2009 and submitted it to the Collector.

36) Besides statement of the Tehsildar, the statement of PW Abdul Hamid, the then Naib Tehsildar,
has also been recorded.

He has deposed that on the directions of the Tehsildar, he undertook National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
9 measurements of the land and found that 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai of land belonging to respondent No.1 had come under acquisition but in the records, only 02 kanals 03 marlas and 01 sirsai was shown to have come under acquisition.

entities.text: National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, extra land of 11 marlas and 02 sirsai belonging to respondent No.1 was found to have been acquired.
He further deposed that he submitted his report before the Tehsildar and the same was forwarded to the Collector.
He admitted the contents of the report and identified his signatures thereon.

37) From the foregoing evidence on record, which has remained unrebutted, the only conclusion that can be drawn is that quantum of land of respondent No.1 that was shown to have been acquired in terms of award dated 23.04.2011 was not in tune with the actual position and the quantum of land of respondent No.1 that had actually come under acquisition was 02 kanals 14 marlas and 03 sirsai.
Thus, respondent No.1 was deprived of compensation in respect of 11 marlas and 02 sirsai of land.
The finding of the learned Reference Court in this regard is based on cogent and convincing evidence and the same does not call for any interference by this Court.
38) The next contention is with regard to quantum of compensation assessed by the Reference Court.
In this regard, the learned Reference Court has relied upon the statements of PWs Abdul Gaffar Mir and Ghulam Jeelani.
Both these witnesses have proved the sale transactions with regard to the land situated Village Levdoora.
Both these witnesses have stated that Village Levdoora is situated at some distance from village Shampora where the acquired land is located.
The sale transactions, regarding which both the above named witnesses have deposed, pertain to the year 2001 and 2006.
39) The aforesaid sale transactions pertain to a different village.
Further these transactions relate to a period which is not proximate to the date when the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued by the Collector.
Therefore, reliance placed by the learned Reference Court on these two transactions is misplaced.

The transactions with regard to land situated in a different locality,
pertaining to a period not proximate to the date of declaration under Section 6 of the Act, are of no help in assessing the market value of the land in terms of the provisions of the Act.
Thus, the learned Reference Court could not have placed reliance upon statements of these two witnesses for assessing the market value of the land in question.
40) There is, however, another aspect of the matter which is required to be considered.
The learned Reference Court has also placed reliance upon the report of the Tehsildar concerned, which he had submitted before the Collector during the acquisition proceedings.
As per this report, the market value of the land in the vicinity of the acquired land at the relevant time was Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.
This report has been referred to by the Collector in his award dated 23.04.2011.

It has been noted in the award that the Tehsildar has reported that prevalent market rate of the land in the village on National Highway is Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal and inside the village, the rate of Rs.5.00 lacs per kanal.
However, the Collector has refused to rely upon the report of the Tehsildar on the ground that the rate statement furnished by the Tehsildar is not supported by documentary evidence.
The Collector has also refused to rely upon the sale transactions, reference whereof has been made in the award.
The Collector has, after discussing the position and location of the land in question as also the rate statement furnished by the Tehsildar, adopted a rate of Rs.8.00 lacs per kanal.

sentences.text: So far as the position and location of the land is concerned, the Collector has noted in the award that town of Qazigund is far developed due to construction of main Railway Station nearby and that the rates of land in the area, particularly along the National Highway have enhanced and nobody is ready to part with the land at any cost.
It has also been noted that whole town is a centre of business activity of all kinds which is the main cause for enhancement of rates of land.

After noticing these features, the Collector has indicated in the award that the proposed land coming under acquisition is also located on either side of the National Highway and if left from acquisition can be converted into residential and commercial establishment.

42) From the above observations of the Collector, it is clear that he is satisfied that the land in question has great commercial potential being located on either side of the National Highway in town Qazigund within Municipal limits.
He has also noted that as per the rate statement furnished by Tehsildar, the market value of the land in question is Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.
The Collector has not even referred to a single fact that would diminish the market value of the land in question.
He has not referred to any material that would have persuaded him to differ with the rate statement furnished by the Tehsildar concerned.
In spite of this, the Collector has adopted a rate of Rs.8.00 lacs per kanal without giving any reason for the same.

43) In fact, record of the Collector shows that vide his letter dated 08.01.2010 addressed to the Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir, he has made it clear that even the rate of Rs.16.00 lacs is not acceptable to the land owners.

In the same communication it has been highlighted by the Collector that the rates of land in the area, particularly along National Highway have increased very high and nobody is ready to part with the land at any cost.

Thus, it is clear that the Collector was satisfied that the rate statement given by the Tehsildar projected the actual market value of the land in question but in spite of this, he has recommended a lesser market value of the land i.e. Rs.8.00 lacs per kanal.

The Tehsildar in his capacity as Government official in discharge of his duties had submitted a report wherein he has stated that the prevalent market rate of the land in the village on National Highway is Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.
In the absence of any material or reasoning, it was not open to the Collector 44)

In view of the above, there was sufficient material on record before the Reference Court to conclude that the market value of the acquired land belonging to respondent No.1 was Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.
The learned Reference Court has, therefore, rightly enhanced the market value of the acquired land belonging to respondent No.1 from Rs.8.00 lacs to Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.
The said conclusion does not call for any interference by this Court.
45) For the foregoing reasons, I do not find any ground to interfere with the impugned award passed by the learned Reference Court.
The appeal lacks merit and is dismissed accordingly.
46) The record be returned back.

(Sanjay D  Judge  Srinagar,
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/

opennyai_summary.issue:
The Reference Court vide order dated 13.05.2015 framed the following issues:
(I) Whether the petitioner was owner and possession of land measuring 2 kanals 14 marlas and 3 sarsaie under survey No.133/133 min, 135/135 min, 134/134 min and 136/136 min situated in village Shampora Qazigund acquired for four lanning of National Highway by Collector?
OPP (II) Whether petitioner, being owner of land comprising of survey Nos.134/134 min and 136/136 min has not been awarded compensation thereof?
OPP (III) Whether the petitioner is entitled to get compensation at the rate of Rs.1.20 lacs per marla for his acquired land?
OPP (IV) Whether reference in hand is not maintainable in the present form and is liable to be rejected?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13) A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of UP Awas Evam Vikas Parishad vs.
Gyan Devi & Ors, (1995) 2 SCC 326, while, considering the provisions contained in Section 50(2) of 1894 Act, concluded that a local authority, for whom the land is being acquired, has a right to participate in the proceedings for acquisition before the Collector as well as before the Reference Court and to adduce evidence for the purpose of determining the amount of compensation and the said right imposes an obligation on the Collector as well as the Reference Court to give a notice to the local authority with regard to the pendency of those proceedings and the date on which the matter regarding determination of amount of compensation would be taken up.
Thus, the Indenting Department is a proper party in the proceedings before the Collector as well as before the Reference Court and it is entitled to be impleaded as a party in the proceedings before the Reference Court.
14)
17) The Supreme Court in para (22) of the same judgement has explained the right of a local authority to file an appeal, in the following manner:
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
4 22.
In case the amount of compensation has been enhanced by the court and no appeal is filed by the Government the local authority if adversely affected by such enhancement may file an appeal with the leave of the court.
This right of the local authority does not depend on its being impleaded as a party in the proceedings before the reference court.
Even if the local authority is not impleaded as a party before the reference court it can file an appeal against the award of the reference court in the High Court after obtaining leave if it is prejudicially affected by the award.
In case the Government files an appeal against the enhancement of the award the local authority is entitled to support the said appeal and get itself impleaded as a party.
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
5 6.
20) Section 52 of the Act, which relates to appeals, clearly provides that an appeal shall lie to the State High Court from any part of the award of the Court and the right of filing of appeal would be subject to the provisions of law in force relating to the procedure in civil section applicable to appeals from original decrees, which means that the procedure prescribed in Civil Procedure Code in respect of the appeals from original decrees would be applicable to such appeals.
Thus, provisions contained in Section 96 and Order 41 of the CPC would be applicable in relation to appeals against the award of Reference Court.
As per these provisions of CPC, a party to a suit has a right to file an appeal.
On the analogy of these provisions, a party before the Reference Court is vested with a right to file appeal against the award passed by the Reference Court without seeking leave of the Court.
Once an objection with regard to limitation is raised by a party before the Reference Court,
an issue in this regard has to be framed and the Reference Court has to address this issue on merits.
Merely, because a reference has been made by the Collector does not mean that the delay stands condoned.
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
7 28)
As per the provisions contained in Section 18 of the Act, an application for reference has to be made within six weeks from the date of Collector's award, if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when the award is made.
In other cases, it has to be made within six weeks of the receipt of notice from the Collector or within six months from the date of Collector's award.
29) In the instant case, respondent No.1 made an application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference, on 10th July, 2013, which is beyond the period of six months, the outer limit provided under Section 18 of the Act.
There is nothing in the record to suggest that respondent No.1, the land owner, was present before the Collector at the time of passing of the award.
Thus, neither copy of the award was endorsed to him nor he was present at the time of passing of the award.
31) Section 12(2) of the Act casts a duty upon the Collector to give notice of the award to those interested persons who are not either personally present or represented before him at the time of making of award.
The period of six months prescribed in Section 18 of the Act in the case of a person who was not present before the Collector at the time of making of award, either in person or through his agent, would commence from the actual or constructive knowledge of making of the award.
Mere knowledge of pendency of acquisition proceedings or of notifications under Section 4 and 6 or any public notice would not mean notice of making of the award.
On facts, it is established that the application for making a reference was definitely made within six months from the date of the knowledge of the award and the reference made by the Collector, Land Acquisition, cannot be held to be barred by time under Section 18 of the Act, as vouched strenuously by appellants, counsel, Mr.
National Highway Authority vs Gh. Nabi Parray & Others on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106728882/
8 B.S. Manhas, in his debate during arguments.
32) From the foregoing analysis of law on the subject, it is clear that in the absence of any evidence to show that a land owner making reference had the knowledge of the essential contents of the award, the knowledge to such land owner shall be attributed only when the amount of compensation has been offered to him.
33) In the instant case, as already indicated, neither the award was made in presence of respondent NO.1 nor any notice was given to him in terms of Section 12(2) of the Act, as such, it cannot be stated that the time of filing application for reference would run against him from the date of the award.
The knowledge of making the award can be attributed to respondent No.1 only when the Collector offered him the compensation assessed under the award.
It is not discernible from the record of the Collector as to when the compensation was offered to respondent No.1.
The burden of proof regarding issue of maintainability of the reference as framed by the Reference Court, was upon the appellant, as such, it was for the appellant to prove that the reference was time barred.
In view of the above, there was sufficient material on record before the Reference Court to conclude that the market value of the acquired land belonging to respondent No.1 was Rs.16.00 lacs per kanal.

The appeal lacks merit and is dismissed accordingly.
